speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your gait and limb ataxia, could you please tell me when these symptoms first started and whether they have been progressing gradually or suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, the ataxia is notably worse on your right side. Have you noticed any other symptoms, such as slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that history. Natalizumab use significantly raises the concern for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), which often presents with focal neurological deficits and ataxia. Have you experienced any recent changes in your vision, such as blurriness or blind spots, or any cognitive changes like memory loss or confusion?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of natalizumab use, focal weakness, and ataxia is highly suspicious for PML, so I will order an MRI to look for characteristic white matter lesions. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI
